corrections_made_during_this_run: The model was written and run standalone in Python before any drawing code existed, and two bugs were caught there rather than in the browser: the generate bit was computed as (a >> i) & 1 & b, which Python parses as a & (1 & b), so every generate bit was wrong; and the unrolled carry multiplied one propagate term too many for the last summand, so the unrolled formula disagreed with the recurrence.

The delay model was restated. The lesson first claimed the textbook 'carry 2n, last sum 2n + 1', which the page's own depth model does not produce: with the external carry in arriving at level 0, the carry out of column i costs two levels and a sum bit one more, so the last sum bit settles at 2n - 1, one level BEFORE the final carry. The model function rippleDepths() was written, the claim was replaced everywhere it appeared (timeline, GATE patterns, revision sheet) and the check now derives both numbers for n = 1..32. A check that asserted 2n = 2n was also removed: it proved nothing.

The hazard simulator first evaluated every gate from the current level's values, which is a zero-delay evaluation and produced no glitch at all (trace 1 1 1 1 1 1). It now reads the previous level, and the trace is 1 1 1 0 1 1.

The hazard check was written against a five-level trace; the corrected simulator emits six levels, so the assertion was rewritten as an invariant (exactly one zero, at level 3, with 1 on both sides) rather than a magic string.
A duplicated assignment in addSub computed the complemented operand twice, the first time with a precedence bug; the dead line was removed.
